providers.reason: Airbus maintains a strong bullish outlook backed by a €5 billion share buyback program running through November 6, 2026. Despite minor quality flaws reported in A321neo components, the company reaffirmed its 870-jet delivery target for 2026, and new mid-term targets suggest a near doubling of profits by 2029.
providers.risk: Persistent supply chain bottlenecks or engine availability issues may hinder the aggressive H2 delivery ramp-up required to meet annual targets.

providers.reason: Reclaimed the 200-day line and sits above its 5/20/50-day averages with a neutral RSI (~55) after Q3. FY26 guidance was reaffirmed (~870 deliveries, ~€7.5bn adjusted EBIT) and BofA raised its target, leaving room for a relief bounce.
providers.risk: Soft Q3 margin (adjusted EBIT -9%) on engine/A350 supply constraints and Spirit integration costs; with fair value near €186, upside may stall without fresh delivery data.

providers.reason: Share buyback program ending Nov 6 provides near-term price support. Strong structural tailwind from EU defense spending (€454B in 2026, €1.5B Defense Industry Programme). Analyst target €232 implies 20% upside despite Q3 delivery challenges.
providers.risk: Supply chain constraints may prevent record Q4 deliveries needed to hit 870 aircraft target, potentially triggering guidance cut.

providers.reason: 9M revenue €50.6bn +7% with EBIT Adjusted €4.5bn, net orders 1,105 vs 514 and backlog 9,310; Buy/Outperform targets €227-€240 with confirmed ~870 delivery target support momentum.
providers.risk: Must deliver ~323 jets in Q4 (~108/month vs ~61 average) to hit 870; any delivery miss or supply-chain warning could quickly reverse momentum.
